units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 5:3">Ab. Zar. V, 3</cite> <he>כדי שישתום ויִסְתּוֹם ויגוב</he>, v. <cite ref="N00115"><he>נָגַב</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:5">B. Mets. VII, 5</cite> <he>שלא יהא … ויהא סוֹתֵם את הפתח וכ׳</he> that he (the laborer) must not be greedy so as to shut the door before himself (make himself objectionable to employers).
<cite ref="Chullin 43a">Ḥull. 43ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מרה שניקבה וכבד סוֹתַמְתָּהּ</he> if the bladder of the gall is perforated, and the liver (adhering to the perforated spot) closes it up.
<cite ref="Chullin 49b:6">Ib. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>חלב טהור סותם</he> clean fat (such as it is permitted to eat) forms a stopper (to an adjacent organ, and makes the animal so affected permitted).

<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 4:9">Pes. IV, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 56a:3">56ᵃ</cite>) <he>ס׳ מי גיחון וכ׳</he> he stopped up the water of the upper Gihon (<cite ref="II Chronicles 32:3">II Chr. XXXII, 3</cite>); a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="O01686"><he>סָתוּם</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="O01687"><he>סְתוּמָה</he></cite>; pl. <he>סְתוּמִים</he>, <he>סְתוּמִין</he>; <he>סְתוּמוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Yevamot 71b">Yeb. 71ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 30b">Nidd. 30ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 14">Lev. R. s. 14</cite> <he>נפתח הס׳ ונסתם וכ׳</he> the organ which (in the embryonic stage) was closed, opens, and that which was open, closes itself.

<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 4:3">Bets. IV, 3</cite> <he>בית … ס׳</he> a room filled with fruit which was closed up (with bricks). Y. ib. 62ᶜ bot. <he>לפסים ס׳</he> pots with their lids on (not yet cut apart); Tosef. ib. III, 13; <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 16:13">Tosef. Sabb. XVI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 17:13">XVII</cite>), 13.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 94a:4">Snh. 94ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>לסרבה</he>, <cite ref="Isaiah 9:6">Is. IX, 6</cite>) <he>מפני מה כל מ״ם … וזה ס׳</he> why is every Mem in the middle of a word open, and this one is closed (final Mem).

Meg. 3ᵃ פתוחין … וס׳ בסוף וכ׳ open in the middle of words and closed at the end (v. מנצפ״ך); a. fr.—Esp. פרשה סתומה a paragraph in the Torah separated from the preceding by a vacant space in the middle of the line, opp. to פתוחה a section beginning a new indented line.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 96">Gen. R. s. 96</cite>, beg., v. infra.

<cite ref="Tractate Soferim 1:14">Treat. Sof’rim I, 14</cite> <he>איזוהי ס׳ כל שהניח וכ׳</he> what is a closed paragraph? When space is left &c.; <he>וכמה יניח … ותהא נקראת ס׳</he> and how much space must be left …, in order that the paragraph may be called closed?; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to conceal. Gen. R. l. c. (ref. to the section beginning with Gen. XLVII, 28) that paragraph is closed, שס׳ ממנו וכ׳ because the Lord concealed from his vision all (coming) troubles; (Yalk. ib. 154 שנסתמו ממנו, v. infra); a. e.—Part. pass. as ab. concealed, not explicitly stated, opp. מפורש.
units: <cite ref="Zevachim 53a:13">Zeb. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>יִלָּמֵד ס׳ מן המפורש</he> let that which is not explicitly stated in a law be derived (by analogy) from what is explicitly stated; Sifra Aḥăré, beg. <he>יְלַמֵּד פתוח על הס׳</he> let the explicit statement throw light on the implicit.
Meg. 15ᵃ כל … אבותיו ס׳ a person (mentioned in the Bible) whose deeds and the deeds of whose ancestors are not stated; a. fr.—Y. Bets. l. c. (in Chald. dict.) סתומה the anonymous opinion, v. סְתָמָא.

senses.gloss: , Nithpa. נִסְתַּתֵּם to be closed; to be concealed; to be silenced. Gen. R. l. c. בקש … ונ׳ ממנו Jacob wanted to reveal the end of the captivity, and it was closed before him; Yalk. ib. l. c. נִסְתְּמוּ ממנו, v. supra.
units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:4">Cant. R. to I, 4</cite> <he>היה אומר … ומִסְתַּתְּמִין</he> he said a word (of charm) over them, and they became silent (dumb).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 31b:5">Snh. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם … עד שיִסְתַּתֵּם טענותיו</he> (Alf. <he>שיִסְתּוֹם</he>; Asheri <he>שיסתיר</he>) he may continually bring evidence and refute, until he declares himself closed as to his pleas, i.e., until he declares that he has no more evidence to offer.

<cite ref="Yevamot 76a">Yeb. 76ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Yevamot 10:4">Tosef. ib. X, 4</cite>, a. e. <he>נ׳ כשר</he> if the perforation in the membrum has closed itself again, he is considered unblemished.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:8">Kel. XIV, 8</cite> <he>נִסְתַּתְּמוּ נקבין</he> if the holes have been stopped up.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 94a:5">Snh. 94ᵃ</cite> <he>לכך נ׳</he> therefore the Mem was closed (the final <cite ref="M00000"><he>מ</he></cite> was written).
<cite ref="Sotah 13b:18">Sot. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>נסתתמו ממנו שערי וכ׳</he> the gates of wisdom were closed before him (he lost his judicial judgment); a. e.

senses.gloss: to close. Y. Snh. X, 28ᶜ bot. היו … מְסַתְּמִין וכ׳ the ministering angels closed the windows (of heaven) that the prayer of Manasseh might not rise; Deut. R. s. 2; (Pesik. Shub., p. 162ᵇ סוֹתְמִין).
